messages.subject: graphics help
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Jeff and others:

Thank you for this fantastic package. In the past I used it a lot to
visualize and share my gene expression data. I made the images with
GDD.

Now I am trying to get it running again on a new machine with the
latest versions but I can't seem to put all the pieces together. The
machine is running Ubuntu 9.04. I've installed the latest version of
RApache and the latest (according to apt-get) libcairo2-devel and
apache. R version 2.9.1 is running. RApache works fine (at least r-
info returns a detailed page). But the graphics don't seem to work.

Here is my R script:

library(Cairo)
setContentType("image/png")
Cairo(file=stdout())
plot(rnorm(100),rnorm(100),col=2)
dev.off()
OK

Instead of a PNG I get the error
Error in Cairo(file = stdout()) :
  file must be a filename. to support writing to a connection,
recompile R and Cairo with the R Connection Patch.

I can't seem to find any more information about this. Do I really need
to recompile R and Cairo? How do I get the R Connection Patch?

Thank you for your help,

Brad

Michel Barbosa wrote:
> Hi Jeff,
>
> I just read about Rapache and it seems very promising. I'm about to
> get started with it, any help I can provide? For example, testing etc?

Hy Michel,

Thanks for the offer. If you'd like to tackle testing issues, there are
two areas where your help can be applied:

1. Various make targets like 'make itest', 'make valgrind', and 'make
gdb' work very well interactively, however they could be tightened up a
bit. For instance, after calling 'make itest' a message is produced that
states you should point your browser to a localhost/port combo to start
testing with the links provided in an index.html file. Essentially, I've
crafted a rudimentary set of tests that link off that page to exercise
many important aspects of rapache, but they could be combed through and
enhanced, and new tests can be added if necessary.

2. A more ambitious automated testing framework would be nice such that
a browser is not needed. This may depend on using a command-line browser
such as wget, or even a web client written in R.

Anyways, thanks for your interest and let the list know what kinds of
issues you run into in just getting started. Compiling and installing
rapache can be daunting.

Best,

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Brad Friedman wrote:
> Hi, Jeff and others:
>
> Thank you for this fantastic package. In the past I used it a lot to
> visualize and share my gene expression data. I made the images with
> GDD.
>
> Now I am trying to get it running again on a new machine with the
> latest versions but I can't seem to put all the pieces together. The
> machine is running Ubuntu 9.04. I've installed the latest version of
> RApache and the latest (according to apt-get) libcairo2-devel and
> apache. R version 2.9.1 is running. RApache works fine (at least r-
> info returns a detailed page). But the graphics don't seem to work.
>
> Here is my R script:
>
> library(Cairo)
> setContentType("image/png")
> Cairo(file=stdout())
> plot(rnorm(100),rnorm(100),col=2)
> dev.off()
> OK
>
> Instead of a PNG I get the error
> Error in Cairo(file = stdout()) :
>   file must be a filename. to support writing to a connection,
> recompile R and Cairo with the R Connection Patch.
>
>
> I can't seem to find any more information about this. Do I really need
> to recompile R and Cairo? How do I get the R Connection Patch?

The best I can recommend is to use either R compiled with cairo support
or Cairo, and you will also want to utilize the sendbin() function.

Sadly, the R Connection Patch never went anywhere with R Core simply
because it would not work across R supported platforms, e.g. Mac,
Windows, and UNIX/Linux. I hope someone can look into it and make the
necessary changes, because it would be nice to have.

Here's the sendbin.r script that you can use as a workaround (comes
bundled with rapache dist located in the test dir):

setContentType("image/png")
t <- tempfile()
png(t,type="cairo")
plot(rnorm(10))
dev.off()
sendBin(readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info <http://file.info>(t)$size))
unlink(t)
DONE

Best,

Jeff

messages.subject: ROutputErrors wrong ContentType
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for making rapache, it's a really cool toy.

I turned on ROutputErrors in my httpd.conf, and it works, but the
output to the browser has ContentType text/plain, so it doesn't get
rendered as HTML. It should probably be text/html. It could be good to
declare an encoding, but I don't know if you can guarantee one if you
ever decide to output user-side variables.

It'd be even nicer if the output was valid HTML, but that's not
strictly necessary for a debugging tool.

P.S. No promises, but I hope to make an RPM spec for rapache for
CentOS 5.

I see no reason why not. I guess the presumption is that if the user
wants to output errors to the browser, and they are formatted in html,
then they want it rendered as such. I'll just have to see if it's okay
to call the apache API function ap_set_content_type() multiple times, as
the R programmer may have already called the R function setContentType()
(which calls ap_set_content_type()).

Plus I need to research if the entire rapache response is buffered
before sending to the browser (shame on me for not knowing!). Many of
you PHP programmers may remember when by default PHP would NOT buffer
output, then when you went to set the content-type you'd get the message
"Cannot add header information - headers already sent".

Hope that makes sense.

> for RMySQL?

Not really. Use the R-sig-db mailing list. Also, check out my RMySQL
maintainer homepage here:

Best,

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
(Apologies for an R noob question, but it came up in the context of
rapache, so the answer may be interesting to other rapache users.)

In PHP, it's pretty easy to handle non-unique parameter names:

/my.php?arr[]=val1&arr[]=val2&arr[]=val3

$ary = $_GET["arr[]"];

cf. http://snipplr.com/view/4444/passing-an-array-through-get-request/

With rapache, GET contains all the `arr[]` parameters, but... how do I
get at them?

messages.subject: upgrading R or Apache
messages.body_plain:
Something I have wondered for a while: When apache + R + rapache are
installed on a machine, and R or Apache is updated, should I also re-
compile and re-install RApache? Or can R binaries be updated without
affecting RApache?

Jeroen

messages.subject: Re: upgrading R or Apache
messages.body_plain:
Jeroen wrote:
> Something I have wondered for a while: When apache + R + rapache are
> installed on a machine, and R or Apache is updated, should I also re-
> compile and re-install RApache? Or can R binaries be updated without
> affecting RApache?

You know, that's a good question. Theoretically, if no R data structures
were altered in a new R version, then the rapache library mod_R.so
should still be binary compatible.

But I still re-compile and re-install rapache after I 'apt-get update
r-*'. Yet another reason to create binary packages of rapache.

Jeff
